official_measurement_examples.name: Historic landfill definition
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Environment Agency dataset defines a historic landfill as a known landfill where no environmental permit is currently in force; the Environment Agency is not the regulator for historic landfills.

official_measurement_examples.name: Dataset incompleteness
official_measurement_examples.fact: Much pre-licensing historic-landfill information derives from early-1990s surveys and the national dataset may be incomplete, so absence is not proof no historic waste disposal occurred.

official_measurement_examples.name: Update frequency lag
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic landfill data is updated every six months while current authorised landfill data has a different update cycle; a surrendered or revoked site can move between layers with timing lag.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current authorised landfill
official_measurement_examples.fact: The authorised-landfill polygon layer represents sites currently authorised by the Environment Agency under environmental permitting regimes; it is distinct from historic landfill evidence.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning versus permit
official_measurement_examples.fact: Waste planning authorities decide land-use location while the Environment Agency controls environmental permitting; either process must not be used as a proxy for the other.

official_measurement_examples.name: Surrender not no residual risk
official_measurement_examples.fact: Permit surrender follows aftercare and risk evidence; surrender or closure does not mean historic waste, landfill gas, leachate or ground-condition issues cease to exist automatically.

official_measurement_examples.name: Recovery permit limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A waste recovery plan or in-principle waste type assessment does not guarantee that waste will be authorised in a site-specific permit.

official_measurement_examples.name: Boundary limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: National landfill polygons are regulatory or historic dataset boundaries and do not establish cadastral ownership, exact waste extent, contamination severity or development yield.

core_rules: historic landfill means no current environmental permit in force
historic landfill absence is not proof no historic waste exists
historic and authorised landfill layers must remain distinct
layer transition can lag after surrender or revocation
waste planning permission is distinct from environmental permit
environmental permit is distinct from planning permission
permit surrender is not proof of zero residual environmental risk
aftercare continues until surrender requirements are met
recovery-plan acceptance is not site permit approval
landfill polygon is not cadastral title geometry
landfill data does not quantify parcel development yield
historic records retain licence and date context
operational status must not be inferred from one stale layer
contamination and landfill-gas assessment remain proposal-specific
no parcel landfill clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Environment Agency, National Data Library and GOV.UK sources checked on 2026-07-26. May-June 2026 landfill datasets and surrender/recovery guidance were retained with current/historic/permit/planning/aftercare separation; no parcel promotion.
